Note: shell env takes precedence over .env (see issue).

gitignore docs: "A gitignore file specifies intentionally untracked files that Git should ignore. Files already tracked by Git are not affected"; "To stop tracking a file that is currently tracked, use git rm --cached". The ledger text is right, but the lesson (section 6) says `.gitignore` "only stops Git from tracking the file from now on" — .gitignore never stops tracking a tracked file.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Actually `.gitignore` has no effect on a file Git already tracks, and it changes nothing in past commits: every commit that ever contained the file still does, and anyone who clones the repository can read the old version.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Execution in examples/don-hang at stage-1: `git log --oneline -- .env` printed nothing (exit 0); `git log --all --oneline -- .env | wc -l` -> 0.

Code inspection at stage-1: Program.cs l.23-39 validates tokens with `new SymmetricSecurityKey(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(signingKey))` from `Jwt:SigningKey`; ValidIssuer/ValidAudience come from committed appsettings.json (`donhang-api`/`donhang-app`), so the key is the only non-public input — holder can sign a token with any `sub`. Connection string uses Username=donhang with the password to reach the donhang database.

Security practice, not a documented behaviour of a pinned version. Nearest official text found: Docker docs best-practices "Be cautious about including sensitive data in environment variables." The mechanism the lesson uses to justify it (Git keeps committed versions) is verified under claim 4. No doc in versions.yaml roots states "replace when leaked"; kind is opinion so not blocking.

issues.text: Wrong mechanism. .gitignore does not stop Git tracking a file that is already tracked; git docs: "Files already tracked by Git are not affected" (you need git rm --cached). The sentence teaches the opposite of the ledger's claim 4.
issues.quote: Actually `.gitignore` only stops Git from tracking the file from now on; every commit that ever contained it still does.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Actually `.gitignore` has no effect on a file Git already tracks, and it changes nothing in past commits: every commit that ever contained the file still does."

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and too strong: .gitignore lists intentionally untracked files to ignore; it does not affect already-tracked files, and `git add --force` adds ignored files (git-add docs: "will not add ignored files by default. You can use the --force option").
issues.quote: a file listing paths Git must not track, so they are never added to a commit by accident.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: "`.gitignore` — a file listing untracked paths Git should ignore, so `git add` does not pick them up by accident." and add the statement to claims (source: git-scm gitignore, git-add).

issues.text: Unlisted claim, absolute: ignored paths can still be force-added, and a path that was committed before being ignored stays tracked. Contradicts the lesson's own section 6 point.
issues.quote: Git never tracks `.env` or anything under `secrets/`.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Git ignores `.env` and everything under `secrets/`, so `git add` does not pick them up." and cover it in the claim for .gitignore.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, inaccurate: `git log -- <path>` shows commits that are not TREESAME for the path (i.e. that added, changed or deleted it) on the current history, not every commit that contained it. For the purpose (was .env ever committed on this branch) the command works, but the description is wrong.
issues.quote: Run `git log --oneline -- .env` to list every commit that ever contained `.env`.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Run `git log --oneline -- .env` to list every commit on this branch that added, changed or deleted `.env`." Add to claim 5 with source git-scm git-log (History Simplification).

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and not true of the lab the lesson then shows: the API never reads `.env`; Compose reads `.env` and the API reads environment variables. A junior will map "the program" to the API.
issues.quote: The program that needs the value reads it from there when it starts
issues.fix: Replace with: "When the program starts, its value is read from there and handed to it, so every developer gets a working value without anyone committing one." (or name Compose explicitly: "Compose reads it from there and hands it to the program as an environment variable").

issues.text: Unlisted, over-general "anything": `docker compose config --no-interpolate` prints the file without substituted values, and not every config view includes secrets. The supportable statement is limited to commands that print the resolved config.
issues.quote: Anything that shows config shows secrets with it.
issues.fix: Replace with: "A command that prints the full resolved config shows the secrets in it too." (matches summary line 5 and the compose config reference).

issues.text: Missing condition: per Compose precedence, a variable from the shell environment wins over `.env`. If the learner's shell exports POSTGRES_PASSWORD or JWT_SIGNING_KEY, Try it step 3 will not show the .env values.
issues.quote: it replaces `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}` and `${JWT_SIGNING_KEY}` with the values from `.env`.
issues.fix: Append: "(unless your shell already sets a variable with the same name, which takes precedence)" and extend claim 3 with the precedence list from variable-interpolation.md.
